To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the interplay of biotic and environmental parameters controlled the development and diversity of pre-salinity crisis microbialites; (2) the microbial community that formed these microbialites changed from thrombolite-generators to stromatolithe-generators as environmental conditions changed; and (3) the diversity of microstructures in microbialites is the result of complex interactions between microbial communities, hydrodynamics, grain supply and hydrochemistry.

the diversity of macro- (i.e., body size), meso- (i.e. thrombolite vs stromatolite), and microstructure (i.e., agglutinated vs. micritic) of pre-salt Messinanian microbialites of Mallorca (Spain) was controlled by a complex inter-play between depositional, hydrological and biotic parameters, which offers insights for the paleo-ecological interpretation of microbialites in general.

the interplay between biotic (microbes) and environmental conditions (hydrodynamics, hydrochemistry, grain supply) is the main factor controlling the diversity of macro, meso and microstructures of microbialites, at any scale, in any environment and throughout geological time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the microbialites that predate the salinity crisis in the Messinian (Upper Miocene) of Mallorca (Spain).

the interplay of environmental conditions (e. g., salinity, grain supply, hydrochemistry) and microbial community composition in the development of the pre-Messinian microbialites from Mallorca, Spain.
the study of microbialite formation in the context of a shallow marine, restricted, hypersaline environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay between biotic, environmental and hydrological conditions, and the resulting complex interplay among them, are crucial to understand microbialite formation.

the Messinian microbialite record of Mallorca is the result of a complex interplay of environmental conditions, which are recorded in the sedimentary record by a wide variety of macro-, mesoscopic- and microstructures.
microbialites are the product of complex interactions between microbial communities, environmental conditions and the depositional setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microbialites are the product of the interaction between microbial communities and the environment in which they lived.
the microbialites of this study record the interaction of biotic and environmental factors in the development of the microbialites, with the latter playing a major role.
the interplay between the biotic and the environmental controls is the key for the development of these microbialites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

microbialites can be a useful proxy for reconstructing palaeoenvironmental conditions, including palaeosalinity and relative sea-level fluctuations, and for interpreting the palaeoceanographic evolution of restricted basins.

, despite being a relatively simple system in terms of lithofacies, the Mallorca microbialites provide an excellent example of how complex interactions between biotic and abiotic parameters can shape microbialite evolution.
microbialite growth is not only influenced by environmental conditions but also by biotic factors.
